scope.surface: Narrow editor-first file detail with source tokens and Back return

productLossClosed: Lynx-for-Web no longer lays each semantic source token out as a separate block. Token hosts and their inner boxes now rejoin the parent text inline formatting context, so source reads as continuous code lines instead of token-boundary fragments.
The fix is scoped to Browser Preview compatibility. The shared file data, tokenization, Native JSX, editing state, save coordinator, and production Native bundle are unchanged.

The existing Back action was already the correct product return path. Final dark and light captures open PORT_WORKFLOW.md through real pointers, expose matching 28x28 Back controls, and return both clients to the Files browser through real pointers.
Wide 1280x820 remains a split detail with a 283px editor and 255/256px explorer, no redundant Back action, real file switching, and zero errors.
remainingResidual: Lynx retains a lightweight six-tone tokenizer instead of the Web Pierre/TextMate editor and therefore does not claim full grammar, selection, or editor-utility parity.

A naive pixel metric rises after the fix because the repaired candidate draws substantially more real source text where the broken candidate left background pixels. The old empty background was not a higher-fidelity editor, so no material residual reduction is claimed from that metric.
Native physical keyboard editing, selection, and save confirmation remain pending-user-session.
harnessMismatch: Before the harness fix, the narrow capture completed its detail gate and dual Back return but retained reachedTargetState=false from an earlier polling phase. The final compositor re-read now admits the state only when the complete fileEditorReady gate passes; switch and return requirements remain independent pass conditions.

One light regression attempt ran concurrently with a wide workbench capture and was rejected before app launch because both tried to reseed the shared .t3-workbench database. The admitted captures run serially and both leak gates remain clean.
diagnosis: The Lynx Text API documents nested text as one inline formatting context.
Lynx OnCall 84860615 records the matching failure mode: wrappers that remain rendered as block or inline-block containers prevent inline text concatenation.
Lynx OnCall 113631289860 confirms nested text becomes inline-text and requires inline-text-compatible styling rather than ordinary box spacing.
classification.evidenceBoundary: Post-commit Browser evidence uses one immutable snapshot, shipping Web and Lynx-for-Web bundles, explicit 360px panel width, dark and light 1024x820 captures, a dark 1280x820 split regression, real file-open and Back pointers, exact geometry, state identity, zero console errors, clean leak gates, and no tracked screenshots. Exact Native independently uses the unchanged production bundle, a generated isolated fixture, measured DevTool touch, main transport, 34px gutter, T3 JetBrains Mono 12px/19px, six token tones, Back return, zero renderer errors, and disposed state.
